title: Bersatu sacks Hamzah Zainudin, three MPs in escalating power struggle
body: KUALA LUMPUR (Feb 13): Parti Pribumi Bersatu Malaysia (Bersatu) has expelled deputy president Datuk Seri Hamzah Zainudin and three dissenting lawmakers amid a deepening power struggle within the party. In a brief statement on Friday, Bersatu secretary general Datuk Seri Mohamed Azmin Ali said the decision to expel Hamzah, the leader of the opposition in the Dewan Rakyat, was made by the party’s disciplinary council, citing a breach of Clause 9.1.4 of the party constitution. The clause requires members to comply with the party constitution as well as its code of ethics and conduct. Hamzah has 14 days from the notice to appeal to the party’s appeals board. At least three other lawmakers were also reportedly sacked under the same clause: Gerik member of Parliament (MP) Fathul Huzir Ayob, Padang Rengas MP Azahari Hasan and Machang MP Wan Ahmad Fayhsal Wan Ahmad Kamal. Wan Ahmad Fayhsal had been suspended since October last year over disciplinary issues. The move comes as cracks within Bersatu’s leadership widen. Hamzah has long been accused of backing efforts to unseat party president Tan Sri Muhyiddin Yassin. The rift intensified over the past week, with the Muhyiddin-aligned faction increasing pressure on Hamzah, including calls for disciplinary action or his removal. Hamzah was reportedly absent from a disciplinary board hearing on Feb 12 as he is currently in Sydney. Earlier on Friday, 16 Bersatu lawmakers issued a joint statement urging Muhyiddin to step down and hand over leadership to Hamzah. Bersatu won 31 parliamentary seats in the 2022 general election, but its representation fell to 25 after six MPs were sacked for supporting Prime Minister Datuk Seri Anwar Ibrahim’s administration. The party later sacked Tasek Gelugor MP Wan Saiful Wan Jan in October last year over disciplinary issues. Following the expulsion of Hamzah and the three MPs, Bersatu is left with 20 seats in the Dewan Rakyat. Hamzah, a veteran politician and four-term Larut MP, will see his next move closely watched amid speculation that Malaysia could face a general election as early as this year. Under Malaysia’s anti-hopping law, Hamzah retains his parliamentary seat as the law does not affect lawmakers expelled from their party. Expelled MPs are also free to join another political party. Umno president Datuk Seri Dr Ahmad Zahid Hamidi is reportedly open to welcoming Hamzah back to the party under the Rumah Bangsa initiative, which aims to unite Malay- and Muslim-based parties under a broad coalition. Hamzah originally switched from Umno to Bersatu after Barisan Nasional lost power in 2018. title: Thai shares, baht set for best week since mid-2025 on election optimism
body: (Feb 13): Thai stocks, as well as the baht, were headed for their best week in more than six months on Friday after last weekend's election boosted hopes for greater political stability, while regional currencies traded slightly lower. The baht has risen 1.8% this week, on track for its biggest weekly gain since May 2025. A decisive election outcome eased fears of a political vacuum and drew foreign investors back into local assets, driving the currency’s rally. The Bhumjaithai Party’s victory further reinforced confidence in policy continuity and political stability, lifting both the currency and equities. "Foreign investors have ramped up their investment in Thai equities since the election result, with total net inflows of about 33 billion baht (US$1.06 billion or RM4.1 billion)," said Poon Panichpibool, market strategist at Krung Thai Bank. Thai shares gained 5.6% this week, eyeing the best week since July 2025. On Friday, the index pared its early gains to trade 0.3% lower. South Korean stocks jumped as much as 1.1% to hit a record high, but pared their gains to close 0.3% lower. For the week, the index has risen just over 8%, marking its best week since January 2021. Singapore shares fell 1.3%, their steepest intraday decline since Oct 23, a day after the city ‑ state’s prime minister said Singapore expects to post a budget surplus of S$8.5 billion in the current fiscal year. For the week, stocks have gained 0.3% set for their eighth consecutive week of gains. Regional currencies depreciated slightly ahead of key US inflation data later in the day, which could set the tone for the dollar. The South Korean won shed 0.6% and the Indonesian rupiah <IDR=> fell 0.2%. The Singapore dollar fell 0.3%. The Malaysian ringgit, which was down 0.3% earlier in the day, pared some of its losses to trade flat. Malaysia's economy grew at its fastest pace in three years in 2025, eclipsing expectations, with momentum likely to continue this year, the central bank said. "The increasing evidence that the economy is not only proving resilient but even outperforming is likely to raise questions over whether the pre-emptive July rate cut last year was necessary," Barclays analysts said. The analysts expect the central bank to hike rates by 25 basis points in May. Taiwan's stock market was closed on Friday for a holiday. title: ECB yet to see full impact of euro appreciation, Kazaks says
body: (Feb 13): The European Central Bank is still waiting to see how severely the economy will be affected by the ascent of the euro that started in 2025, according to Governing Council member Martins Kazaks. With estimates suggesting that it takes approximately 12 months for currency shifts to trickle through, “we will likely see the full impact of the euro’s strengthening last year towards late spring,” Kazaks said in an interview in Riga. The single currency gained 14% in the first half of 2025, as President Donald Trump’s back and forth on trade tariffs undermined confidence in the dollar and raised global uncertainty. The euro continued its rally earlier this year — breaking through US$1.20 for the first time since 2021 — in response to US threats against Greenland. While most of the appreciation is reflected in the ECB’s latest projections that show growth accelerating over time and inflation settling at the 2% target, policymakers including President Christine Lagarde have said they’re watchful and stand ready to respond. Kazaks argued that the current situation doesn’t require any action — and that officials are in “monitoring mode.” “If you will, this is a kind of manifestation of attention,” he said. “It is not a verbal intervention. We are not that far.” But he did express concern that prevailing weakness in the economy makes it harder for businesses and consumers to cope. “My worry is very much that the euro has strengthened over the past year not because the euro-zone economy has gotten stronger but because uncertainty has increased and the US dollar has weakened,” he said. Europe’s problem is one of low competitiveness compared with America and China, which — if addressed — would also raise the economy’s tolerance for a stronger currency. After years of prodding from Lagarde and ECB presidents before her, heads of state are finally inching towards action. They discussed a roadmap towards strengthening the bloc’s fundamentals at a day-long retreat on Thursday. Kazaks, who heads Latvia’s central bank, also said the ECB’s monetary policy settings are currently appropriate — and that risks to its inflation outlook “might still be balanced”. “We are also in a good position to move in any direction if necessary,” he added. “But now is not the time.” The ECB left its deposit rate unchanged at 2% last week and neither economists nor traders expect a move anytime soon. title: MCMC identifies over 50 accounts spreading racially charged CIB content — Fahmi
body: PUTRAJAYA (Feb 13): The Malaysian Communications and Multimedia Commission (MCMC) has identified more than 40 Facebook accounts and nearly 10 TikTok accounts involved in spreading suspected racially charged coordinated inauthentic behaviour (CIB) over the past 24 hours. Communications Minister Datuk Fahmi Fadzil said a video with the same narrative has been circulating, reportedly showing an incident between Indian and Malay individuals. “It was found that over the past 24 hours, a news story went viral, originally claiming that an Indian gangster had attacked a Malay landowner, with subtle racial undertones added. “Nearly all of these posts used the same video and wording. Investigations into the spread of this content are ongoing, and any attempt to fuel racial tension will not be tolerated,” he said. Fahmi, who is also the Madani government spokesperson, told reporters this at a press conference following Friday's Cabinet meeting. On Thursday, police confirmed the viral video of a four-wheel drive hitting a motorcyclist in Kampung Sungai Jernih, Kajang, had no gangster or racial elements. Selangor police chief Datuk Shazeli Kahar said preliminary investigations indicated the incident stemmed from a personal dispute over land and lorry access in the area. Images claiming a threat had been made were tagged with the 16-second video, which had gone viral on social media. In a separate development, Fahmi said MCMC identified 19 suspected fake accounts that spread inappropriate content during a live broadcast of a Parliamentary sitting. “Of the 19 accounts, two have been confirmed as fake, while investigations continue into the remaining 17,” he said, citing a local English-language newspaper report from Feb 8 that said the live broadcast had become a hub for hate speech and misinformation, calling for proactive action. title: June 18 decision on Bersatu's bid to challenge freezing of bank accounts
body: KUALA LUMPUR (Feb 13): The High Court on Friday fixed June 18 to deliver its decision on Parti Pribumi Bersatu Malaysia’s (Bersatu) judicial review application challenging the Malaysian Anti-Corruption Commission’s (MACC) freezing and seizure of two of the party’s bank accounts. Judicial commissioner Datuk Aliza Sulaiman set the date after hearing submissions from lawyer Chetan Jethwani, representing Bersatu, and senior federal counsel Nurhafizza Azizan, who appeared for the government and the MACC. Earlier, Chetan argued that the investigation and criminal charges were directed at former prime minister Tan Sri Muhyiddin Yassin in his personal capacity and bore no connection to Bersatu. In reply, Nurhafizza contended that the investigation and charges against Muhyiddin were brought in his capacity as the Bersatu president, as he was responsible for managing the party’s accounts, pursuant to Section 51(2) of the Societies Act 1966. She submitted that under the provision, office-bearers and individuals involved in the management of a society may be held liable even if they did not directly commit the offence. On Oct 30, 2023, the High Court granted Bersatu leave to commence judicial review proceedings to challenge the MACC’s seizure of two of its bank accounts. The application was filed on May 29, 2023 by Capt (Rtd) Datuk Muhammad Suhaimi Yahya in his capacity as a public officer of the party. He named then attorney general Tan Sri Idrus Harun and MACC chief commissioner Tan Sri Azam Baki as the first and second respondents respectively, along with 20 others as the third to 22nd respondents. Bersatu contended that its CIMB and AmBank accounts were seized on April 19, 2023, without any seizure order being served on the party as required under Section 50(1) of the Anti-Money Laundering, Anti-Terrorism Financing and Proceeds of Unlawful Activities Act 2001. The party further claimed that although the MACC issued a statement on April 20, 2023, saying the accounts had been seized on April 11, it was never notified of the seizure on that date. title: Trump plans to roll back some tariffs on steel and aluminium goods — report
body: (Feb 13): US President Donald Trump plans to scale back some tariffs on steel and aluminum goods, the Financial Times reported on Friday, citing people familiar with the matter. Officials in the Commerce Department and US trade representative’s office believe the tariffs are hurting consumers by raising prices for goods including pie tins and food-and-drink cans, the FT report said. Voters nationwide are worried about consumer prices and cost-of-living concerns are expected to be a major factor for Americans heading into the November mid-term elections. A recent Reuters /Ipsos poll showed that 30% of Americans approved of Trump’s handling of the rising cost of living, while 59% disapproved, including nine in 10 Democrats and one in five Republicans. Trump hit steel and aluminum imports with tariffs of up to 50% last year and has repeatedly used levies as a negotiating tool with a range of trading partners. The Trump administration is now reviewing a list of products affected by the levies and plans to exempt some items, halt the expansion of the lists and instead launch more targeted national security probes into specific goods, the FT report added. The White House and the Commerce Department did not immediately respond to Reuters requests for comment outside of regular business hours. Trump recently touted his economic record in Detroit, aiming to refocus attention on US manufacturing and his efforts to tackle high consumer costs as the White House seeks to show it is addressing the economic anxieties gripping US households. The US Commerce Department last year hiked steel and aluminum tariffs on more than 400 products including wind turbines, mobile cranes, appliances, bulldozers and other heavy equipment, along with railcars, motorcycles, marine engines, furniture and hundreds of other products. title: China's yuan set for longest weekly winning streak in 13 years
body: SHANGHAI (Feb 13): China's yuan dipped on Friday, but is set for a 12th week of gains in its longest winning streak in 13 years, as exporters rushed to bring home receipts from booming trade ahead of the Lunar New Year. Some analysts also see the rising yuan and China's buoyant stock market feeding each other, but say the central bank has enough tools up its sleeves to forestall the currency appreciating too quickly. The onshore yuan changed hands at 6.9068 per dollar around noon, slightly weaker than the previous session's close of 6.9033. The dollar index =USD rebounded 0.03% in Asian trade. For the week, the yuan has gained roughly 0.4% in its best weekly performance this year. It also marked the longest run of weekly gains since late 2012. The recent spurt, which sent the yuan to its firmest level in 33 months on Thursday, was partly fuelled by seasonal dollar selling, but the People's Bank of China (PBOC) appears not in a hurry to step into the market directly, Caitong Securities said in a note. History shows that the PBOC "has a rich toolkit, and can act with precision and restraint to easily cope with possible overshooting." Reflecting its intention to slow the pace of yuan appreciation, the PBOC set the daily guidance rate at 6.9398 per dollar, 350 pips weaker than Reuters estimate. The spot yuan is allowed to trade a maximum of 2% either side of the fixed midpoint each day. Topsperity Securities said that the yuan's strength is also lending support to Chinese stocks. Trading typically thins ahead of the Spring Festival holiday, but the stock market has held at a relatively high level "without pulling back", the brokerage said in a report. title: China's new home prices extend decline as weak demand hounds sector
body: BEIJING (Feb 13): China's new home prices extended their decline in January, as official data painted a familiar picture of a property sector unable to shake off a years-long downturn, maintaining pressure on cash-strapped developers and the broader economy. Investors have been watching for signs of bottoming out in the market, but demand has remained soft despite a raft of policy measures since the industry plunged into crisis in 2021. "The foundations of the property market's recovery remain fragile," said Zhang Dawei, an analyst at Centaline Property. Prices for new homes fell 0.4% month-on-month, matching the previous month's decline, according to Reuters calculations based on data released by the National Bureau of Statistics on Friday. On an annual basis, prices dropped 3.1% in January, quickening from a 2.7% fall in the previous month for the steepest decline in seven months. The prolonged downturn in the property sector, once a key engine of economic growth, has weighed on household wealth as home values have fallen. That has crimped consumption, effectively enfeebling a key engine of growth in the world's second-biggest economy. Policymakers have prioritised reviving consumer spending as they seek to curb industrial overcapacity and cushion China against external trade risks. A rebound in home-buying would also help property developers, many of which need new cash flow to repay debt and finance construction to deliver pre-sold projects. Centaline Property's Zhang said that "problems such as heavy inventories in third-tier cities and weak demand have yet to be fundamentally resolved, and a full improvement in market expectations will take time." In the near term, the pace of month-on-month declines is likely to slow as support measures continue to take effect, he said, but added that smaller cities will need time to work through inventories and unlock demand, keeping prices under pressure. Beijing has rolled out a raft of measures since the 2021 crisis rippled across the economy, including easing purchase restrictions and cutting down-payment requirements. State-owned companies are also buying foreclosed property projects, in a sign that long-promised government efforts to reduce massive oversupply are finally getting traction. But the sector is yet to stage a recovery. Of the 70 cities surveyed by the NBS, 62 posted price declines, up from 58 in the previous month. The resale market remained weak. Month-on-month declines eased slightly, but year-on-year falls accelerated, with prices down 7.6% in tier-one cities and more than 6% in smaller cities. State media reported in late January that authorities had removed the so-called "three red lines" — caps on developers' debt-to-cash, debt-to-assets and debt-to-equity ratios that lenders used when extending new loans. Introduced in 2020, the policy helped trigger a liquidity squeeze across the sector, with many builders defaulting and running short of cash to complete presold homes. Even without the caps, funding strains persist as developers move away from the high-leverage model that powered the boom, analysts say. China's primary property sales are set to fall 10% to 14% in 2026, as an oversupplied market continues to push down prices, S&P Global Ratings said in a research note this week. "In our view, only the government could address oversupply in the property sector, given the scale of this problem. We have yet to see signs that it is keen to intervene." title: BOJ hawk Tamura flags spring as possible timing for rate hike
body: (Feb 13): One of the Bank of Japan’s (BOJ) most hawkish members indicated that conditions for the central bank’s next interest rate hike could be in place by spring, a comment that is likely to fuel further speculation of an early move. “It is quite possible that, as early as this spring, the price stability target of 2% can be judged to have been achieved if it’s confirmed with a high certainty that wage growth this year will be in line with the target for the third consecutive year,” Tamura said Friday in a speech at a business conference in Yokohama. While it’s unclear if the rest of the BOJ board shares Tamura’s view, his remarks suggest that governor Kazuo Ueda will probably face increased opposition if he decides to stand pat at the next policy meetings through April. Tamura’s remarks will also likely feed growing market speculation that the next rate hike will come in April, or as early as next month. Even before Prime Minister Sanae Takaichi’s landslide election victory on Sunday, expectations of a big win for the pro-stimulus premier had generated speculation that the yen would stay at weak levels and keep upward pressure on inflation. Since the BOJ’s last policy gathering in January, BOJ watchers at Barclays and BNP Paribas have shifted their rate calls to April. Traders see around a 75% chance of the BOJ raising its benchmark rate by April, according to overnight swaps, jumping from around 40% a month ago. Tamura defined price stability as a state in which economic agents including households and firms can make decisions regarding consumption and investment without needing to factor in fluctuations in the general level of price growth. That’s largely in line with the common understanding among central bankers. Former Federal Reserve chair Alan Greenspan is known for repeatedly making similar remarks. “However, many households are struggling with the increased cost of living, and many firms are struggling with higher input prices, and I personally do not think it can be claimed that Japan is experiencing price stability as defined,” Tamura said. Japan’s key inflation measure quickened to 3.1% last year, staying above BOJ’s target for four straight years, the longest stretch since 1992. Takaichi’s biggest election win in the post-war era is partly based on her pledge to alleviate the pain of the cost-of-living crunch. Ensuring that the trend in wage growth remains strong is a key concern both for the premier and the BOJ. The central bank sees wage gains as a critical part of generating a stable inflation cycle that feeds into higher consumption and economic growth. The nation’s biggest union federation typically releases its results of annual pay negotiations in mid-March, a key data point that has been followed by central bank moves in the past. Tamura, a former executive at Sumitomo Mitsui Financial Group, is known as a frequent dissenter calling for faster policy normalisation, together with Hajime Takata. At January’s meeting, Takata gave the stand-pat decision a hawkish feel by voting for a back-to-back rate hike. In Tamura’s view, the limited impact on the economy from the hikes towards the current 0.75% rate shows that the bank still has a long way to go before it reaches a level that is neither restrictive nor stimulative for the economy. “There is still considerable distance to the neutral interest rate level,” Tamura said. “In other words, even if the bank raises its policy interest rate, financial conditions will remain accommodative.” The BOJ delivers its next policy decision on March 19, the same day Takaichi is scheduled to meet US President Donald Trump in the US. title: Police seize 98.73kg drug worth RM4.9 mil at Padang Besar
body: KANGAR (Feb 13): Police seized 98.73kg of methamphetamine, estimated to be worth RM4.9 million, following the arrest of a local man in an operation near the General Operations Force (GOF) control post along Jalan KTMB, Padang Besar, last Monday (Feb 9). Perlis police chief Datuk Muhammad Abdul Halim said the 20-year-old suspect was detained at about 9pm during a joint operation by the Narcotics Criminal Investigation Department (JSJN) of the Perlis Police Contingent Headquarters (IPK) and the 1st Battalion of the General Operations Force (PGA) in Ulu Kinta, Perak. “A search of a Proton Saga driven by the suspect uncovered four white sacks containing powder believed to be syabu, weighing 98.73kg and estimated to be worth RM4,936,600. “The quantity seized is estimated to be capable of affecting up to 493,650 individuals if distributed into the market,” he told a press conference at the Perlis IPK on Friday. Muhammad said preliminary investigations indicated that the suspect was believed to have used a “rat trail” along the Malaysia-Thailand border in the Padang Besar district as a smuggling route before distributing the supply to the southern part of the country. He said the suspect attempted to flee during the operation, driving recklessly and endangering the enforcement team, prompting officers to fire a shot at the vehicle’s tyres to safeguard the personnel. “The suspect sustained injuries to his face, hands and legs after crashing into a vehicle used by the raiding team,” he said. Initial urine screening showed the suspect tested positive for ketamine. Checks on his background also revealed previous records related to drug offences. The case is being investigated under Section 39B of the Dangerous Drugs Act 1952. The suspect is on remand from Feb 10 to 16 to assist in investigations. Muhammad added that the Perlis JSJN remains committed to intensifying efforts to curb drug trafficking, particularly in border areas, and urged the public to continue providing information to help combat such activities. title: Court orders ex-SSM chief Zahrah to enter defence for eight graft charges, acquits her of 20 other charges
body: KUALA LUMPUR (Feb 13) : The Sessions Court has ordered former Companies Commission of Malaysia (SSM) chief executive officer Datuk Zahrah Abd Wahab Fenner to enter her defence for a total of eight graft charges. At the same time, Sessions Court judge Azura Alwi, who delivered her decision at the end of the prosecution's case on Friday, freed the 66-year-old Zahrah of a further 20 charges that had been levelled against her as the prosecution's case lacked evidence to prove elements of the charges. The eight amended charges comprise of four charges where Zahrah, as the principal offender, was charged with accepting bribes amounting to RM1.21 million in relation to SSM-related projects. For these charges, she is accused of receiving bribes in exchange for granting advertising contracts to Ikhlas Padu Sdn Bhd and SSJ Niaga. The contracts were for commercial LED signage for the Companies Commission in Johor and Kedah. The charge also comprises of accepting bribes to award a contract to Marikaya Enterprise for their event management services for the 2018 SSM Bizfair Programme in Sabah. These charges are framed under Section 17(a) of the Malaysian Anti-Corruption Commission (MACC) Act and carries a punishment of imprisonment of not more than 20 years, and a fine of not less than five times the bribe or RM10,000, whichever is higher. The other four charges for which Zahrah has to enter her defence is where she abetted her son, Abdulazeez Wan Ruslan, for graft. These charges were framed under Section 28(1)(c) of the MACC Act and carry a punishment of 20 years’ imprisonment, a fine of not less than five times the bribe or RM10,000, whichever is higher. Zahrah was first charged in 2019. Judge Azura however acquitted Zahrah of the other 20 charges against her on the grounds that the prosecution had failed to raise reasonable doubt. "The prosecution failed to present strong evidence to prove the essential facts relating to the receipt of bribe money in all the charges concerned. "In this case, no bribe money was discovered. Although that is not an essential element the prosecution must prove, the court holds that in the circumstances of this case, there must be corroborative and/or circumstantial evidence that is strong and sufficient to establish the receipt of bribe money as alleged in the charges," the judge said. The court also ordered for Zahrah’s son, Abdulazeez, 39, to enter his defence for all graft charges where he was the principal offender. The charges framed under Section 16(a)(A) of the MACC Act carry a punishment of 20 years’ imprisonment, a fine of not less than five times the bribe or RM10,000, whichever is higher. Deputy Public Prosecutor Law Chin How led the team of prosecutors on Friday. Datuk Hasnal Rezua Merican from the Chambers of Kamarul Hisyam & Hasnal Rezua appeared for Zahrah, and Shahir Ab Razak of Shahir Khubayb & Co appeared for her son. title: Govt sets up task force to probe anti-graft chief Azam Baki
body: KUALA LUMPUR (Feb 13): The government has established a special task force to investigate Malaysian Anti-Corruption Commission (MACC) chief commissioner Tan Sri Azam Baki, Communications Minister Datuk Fahmi Fadzil announced on Friday. The task force will be headed by Chief Secretary to the government Tan Sri Shamsul Azri Abu Bakar and will report its findings to the Cabinet for further action, Fahmi said at a news conference after the weekly Cabinet meeting. He added that the suspension of the MACC chief was not discussed during the meeting. Fahmi did not disclose the scope of the taskforce’s investigation and declined to comment on whether a timeline had been set for the task force to submit its findings. The Cabinet’s move comes amid public outrage following a news report on Azam’s outsized shareholdings in publicly listed companies. Bloomberg first reported that he owned 17.7 million shares in financial services firm Velocity Capital Partner Bhd (KL: VELOCITY ). Azam acknowledged purchasing the shares in early 2025 before selling them in July, but maintained that he had acted within the rules. He has also said he is open to fully cooperating with any investigations, while taking legal action against Bloomberg. Another report on Thursday implicated Azam in an alleged collusion with businesspeople to take over local companies. Earlier, eight PKR lawmakers led by former economic minister Datuk Seri Rafizi Ramli called on the top leadership of DAP and Amanah to press for investigations into the allegations against Azam. title: PKR MPs tell DAP, Amanah to push PM for MACC chief's suspension
body: KUALA LUMPUR (Feb 13): Eight PKR lawmakers led by former economy minister Datuk Seri Rafizi Ramli have called on the top leadership of DAP and Amanah to press Prime Minister Datuk Seri Anwar Ibrahim to suspend Malaysian Anti-Corruption Commission (MACC) chief commissioner Tan Sri Azam Baki and investigate allegations against him. At a press conference on Friday, Rafizi singled out DAP, the largest party in the unity government by the number of lawmakers, saying its influence could compel the prime minister to take the matter seriously. “DAP doesn’t have to wait six months to make a decision. This issue is blowing up right now. Use your responsibility, influence and leverage within the government to engage directly and put pressure on Datuk Seri Anwar,” Rafizi said. DAP currently holds 40 parliamentary seats and had previously pledged to accelerate the reform agenda over the next six months, following its heavy defeat in last November’s Sabah election. Rafizi said he and the seven other PKR lawmakers will begin writing to DAP and Amanah leaders next week to push for the suspension and an immediate independent probe. The other PKR members of Parliament supporting this move are Wong Chen (Subang), Rodziah Ismail (Ampang), Nik Nazmi Nik Ahmad (Setiawangsa), Lee Chean Chung (Petaling Jaya), S Kesavan (Sungai Siput), Tan Kar Hing (Gopeng) and Zahir Hassan (Wangsa Maju). Azam has been at the centre of controversy after Bloomberg reported earlier this week that he held shares above the limit allowed for civil servants in Velocity Capital Partner Bhd (KL: VELOCITY ), a publicly listed financial services firm. Azam acknowledged buying the shares in early 2025 and selling them in July, but maintained that he acted within the rules, declaring all financial and asset holdings through official channels. Rafizi said the lawmakers will take a series of steps to ensure the Bloomberg allegations are not dismissed without an independent and transparent investigation. Besides writing to DAP and Amanah leaders, they will also contact all government backbenchers and opposition MPs to seek support for suspending Azam and launching a probe. They urged MPs to return to their constituencies to brief residents on the allegations. The group also plans to reach out to electoral reform body Bersih to propose a peaceful public assembly allowing citizens to express concern over alleged misconduct in the MACC. Rafizi added that he will file a police report against Azam regarding Bloomberg ’s claims that he interfered in a firearms case, allowing the police to investigate. He urged the government, particularly the prime minister, to take the matter seriously and warned it would be “highly unfair” if the Pakatan Harapan coalition or the prime minister were blamed over allegations involving Azam. title: Use of Sawit Intelligent Management System reaches 95% among MPOB licence holders
body: KUALA LUMPUR (Feb 13): More than 95% of Malaysian Palm Oil Board (MPOB) licence holders across various categories have actively used the Sawit Intelligent Management System (SIMS). According to MPOB director general Datuk Ahmad Parveez Ghulam Kadir, the SIMS system has the potential to function as an integrated data hub for the palm oil industry, enabling more efficient and effective monitoring and traceability across the palm oil supply chain. “In the meantime, he said GeoSAWIT is currently being upgraded with the latest geospatial equipment and technology for mapping the coverage of the nation’s oil palm plantations. “The GeoSAWIT control room is located at MPOB headquarters, and the upgrade work is expected to be completed by mid-2026,” he said in his welcome address at the briefing session on SIMS and the GeoSAWIT Platform to Minister of Plantation and Commodities Datuk Seri Dr Noraini Ahmad on Wednesday (Feb 11). The GeoSAWIT platform enables spatial data to support land-use monitoring, risk assessment, and evidentiary support for market compliance requirements. Ahmad Parveez added that GeoSAWIT has been developed with an inclusive, national-scale approach to ensure all categories of producers, especially smallholders, remain part of an increasingly regulated supply chain. “Today’s briefing will focus on SIMS, covering the traceability module and the fleet management module, which monitors the movement of palm oil using tanker trucks, as well as the use of GeoSAWIT through geospatial technology for verification and traceability of oil palm planting to ensure the national palm oil industry remains competitive, transparent and sustainable,” he added. title: Singapore plans regulation for blind boxes over gambling risks
body: (Feb 13): As mania about “mystery” shopping sweeps through the world, Singapore is moving to tackle gambling risks raised by products which conceal their specific contents from shoppers. Singapore’s gambling authorities and home affairs ministry have decided to regulate how such “blind boxes” are offered to the public, according to a written reply to a parliamentary question on Feb 12. While authorities draft new regulations, they will consider standardising and making it mandatory for boxes to disclose the probability of receiving certain products. The move aims to better manage gambling inducement risks, Coordinating Minister for National Security and Minister for Home Affairs K Shanmugam said in the reply. The blind box phenomenon, which has fuelled surges in revenue for toy manufacturers such as Pop Mart International Group Ltd and Miniso Group Holding Ltd, has driven fans to hunt down rare models and resell valuable items for thousands of dollars. Pop Mart has opened at least six stores across Singapore, from the city’s prime shopping district Orchard to suburban malls, and hosts an annual exhibition in the country that draws crowds of hundreds. Tickets to the event sold for as much as S$208 (RM645) for a premium experience in 2025. It remains unclear how the new regulations may affect sales of the popular series. Pop Mart did not respond to Bloomberg’s request for comment. With these plans, Singapore has gone a step further than many other nations in clamping down on similar mystery products that may encourage gambling-like behaviour. In 2023, China Consumers Association called for operators to disclose key information, such as the release quantity and probability of obtaining limited-edition items. China’s People’s Daily previously warned about related products’ impact on children. It raised the idea of establishing so-called minor-only zones as an attempt to dissuade underage buyers from addictive purchasing behaviours. title: Appellate court dismisses Anwar’s press secretary’s appeal in defaming Yusoff Rawther
body: PUTRAJAYA (Feb 13) : A three-member Court of Appeal (COA) bench has on Friday dismissed the appeal by Tunku Nashrul Tunku Abaidah, who is Prime Minister Datuk Seri Anwar Ibrahim’s senior press secretary, over a defamation suit filed by Anwar’s former aide Muhammed Yusoff Rawther in 2019. With this, Tunku Nashrul has been asked to pay RM80,000 and also issue an apology to Yusoff within 45 days from today, as this was his final appeal, following the case that originated from the Sessions Court. Tunku Nashrul had previously obtained a stay from the High Court in order not to issue an apology. COA judge Datuk Wong Kian Kheong, who led the bench in dismissing the appeal, said the decisions of the Sessions Court and High Court are correct, as they had judicially appreciated the matter at hand. Wong said what was published and said in Tunku Nashrul’s statement to the press in June 2019 — accusations that alleged that Yusoff had a discipline problem, that he had been sacked, taken drugs, and that he created his own stories — were not supported as there are no police reports on him. Wong said the statement issued had clearly defamed Yusoff. The court further ruled against the four defences of fair comment, qualified privilege, responsible journalism, and justification that had been pleaded. “These four defences were also dismissed by the Sessions Court and the High Court. “As there is no cross-appeal with regard to the quantum of damages which had been reduced by the High Court, the bench finds the sum to be appropriate. Following this, we dismiss the appellant’s (Tunku Nashrul’s) appeal,” the judge said. Wong, who sat with Datuk Muhammad Firuz Jaffril and Datuk Nadzarin Wok Nordin, also ordered Tunku Nashrul to pay RM30,000 in costs. Initially, the Shah Alam Sessions Court had found Tunku Nashrul guilty of defamation and had awarded Yusoff damages of RM200,000 in October 2022. On appeal at the High Court in May 2023, the quantum was reduced to RM80,000 by judge Khadijah Idris. Yusoff had filed the suit in September 2019, alleging that Tunku Nashrul had damaged his reputation when Tunku Nashrul alleged that he (Yusoff) had a disciplinary problem, took drugs, and that he was sacked when he made allegations that Anwar had sexually assaulted him at his office. Yusoff has also filed a separate suit against Anwar for the alleged sexual assault, which is pending hearing at the High Court. Yusoff was represented by M Thayalan and Fathima Mohd Idris from Messrs Thayalan & Associates, while Muhammad Azwar Ab Manab from Messrs Azwar & Partners appeared for Tunku Nashrul. title: BNP sweeps Bangladesh election, Tarique Rahman set to become PM
body: DHAKA (Feb 13): Bangladesh’s opposition Bangladesh Nationalist Party (BNP) won a landslide parliamentary election on Friday, returning to power after nearly two decades and positioning party leader Tarique Rahman to become prime minister as the country emerges from months of unrest and economic disruption. Rahman, the son of former premier Khaleda Zia who returned to Dhaka in December after nearly two decades abroad, faces immediate challenges in restoring political stability, reviving investor confidence and rebuilding key industries — including the garment sector — after prolonged turmoil that followed the collapse of former prime minister Sheikh Hasina’s government in 2024. The latest counts in a vote viewed as the South Asian nation's first truly competitive election in years gave the BNP and its allies at least 212 of the 299 seats up for grabs, local TV channels said. The opposition Jamaat-e-Islami and its allies won 70 seats in the Jatiya Sangsad, or House of the Nation. The Election Commission put the BNP at 181 seats, the Jamaat-e-Islami at 61 and others at 7, with full official results expected in the next few hours. Results in several seats are still being processed and the full result is expected within hours, the commission said, though the gazette notification will take a few more days, which could delay the swearing-in of the new government. Under the constitution, the new government cannot be sworn in unless the gazette notification reporting the results is released. The BNP thanked its supporters soon after election trends became clear and called for special prayers on Friday for the nation and its people. "Despite winning ... by a large margin of votes, no celebratory procession or rally shall be organised," the party said in a statement. The National Citizen Party (NCP), led by youth activists who played a key role in toppling Hasina, won just five of the 30 seats that it contested. The NCP was part of the Jamaat-led alliance. A clear outcome had been viewed as key for stability in the Muslim-majority nation of 175 million after months of deadly anti-Hasina unrest disrupted everyday life and industries including garment manufacturing. Bangladesh is the No. 2 exporter of garments in the world. "A strong majority gives the BNP the parliamentary strength to pass reforms efficiently and avoid legislative paralysis. That alone can create short-term political stability," said Selim Raihan, an economics professor at the University of Dhaka. In its manifesto, the BNP promised to prioritise job creation, protect low-income and marginal households and ensure fair prices to farmers. "If the factories run regularly and we get our wages on time, that’s what matters to us. I just want the BNP government to bring back stability so more orders come to Bangladesh and we can survive," Josna Begum, 28, a garment worker and mother of two, told Reuters . Indian Prime Minister Narendra Modi, Pakistan Prime Minister Shehbaz Sharif and the US ambassador to Bangladesh, Brent T Christensen, were among the first to congratulate Rahman on his party's victory. The Islamist Jamaat-e-Islami conceded defeat late on Thursday night once trends became clear, but said in a statement on Friday that it was "not satisfied" with the process and asked its followers to remain patient. The party won its highest-ever tally of 70 seats in Parliament, contesting for the first time since it was banned in 2013 after its registration was cancelled. A court in Bangladesh said the party's constitution went against secularism. The ban was lifted after Hasina's ouster. Now in exile in New Delhi, Hasina long dominated Bangladesh politics along with Rahman's mother, while his father was a leading independence figure who ruled from 1977 until 1981 before he was assassinated. The BNP win with more than 200 seats is one of its biggest, surpassing its 2001 victory with 193, although Hasina's Awami League, which ruled for 15 years and was barred from contesting this time, secured a bigger tally of 230 in 2008. But elections of other years were boycotted by one of the main parties or were contentious. Overnight, throngs of supporters cheered and shouted slogans at the BNP headquarters in Dhaka as the scale of the party's landslide became clear. Turnout exceeded the 42% of the last election in 2024, with media reports saying nearly 60% of registered voters participated in the election on Thursday. More than 2,000 candidates, many independents among them, were on the ballot, which featured a record number of at least 50 parties. Voting in one constituency was postponed after a candidate died. Broadcaster Jamuna TV said more than two million voters chose "Yes" while more than 850,000 said "No" in a referendum on constitutional reforms held alongside the election, but there was no official word on the outcome. The changes include two-term limits for prime ministers and stronger judicial independence and women's representation while providing for neutral interim governments during election periods and setting up a second house of the 300-seat parliament. title: Court allows Najib to attend hearing of two appeals
body: PUTRAJAYA (Feb 13): The Court of Appeal on Friday has allowed an application for an order to produce (OTP), which will allow Datuk Seri Najib Razak to attend two proceedings before the court this month and next month. A three-member bench led by Datuk Wong Kian Kheong allowed the application by Najib’s counsel, Wan Muhammad Arfan Wan Othman, for the former prime minister to be present at an appeal hearing for Health Minister Datuk Seri Dr Dzulkefly Ahmad, which is scheduled for Feb 24, and also in Najib’s appeal against a decision not to cite Federal Court judge Tan Sri Ahmad Terrirudin Mohd Salleh for contempt, which is scheduled for March 13. Dr Dzulkefly’s case concerns a defamation suit filed against Najib. The health minister is seeking an appeal to recuse High Court Judicial Commissioner Arziah Mohamed Apandi, who is presiding over the matter. The minister claims in his application that statements Arziah had made during two case management sessions indicate that the case might be struck off if no “out-of-court settlements” were reached. These, he claims, demonstrate bias or created a perception of bias. Arziah in dismissing her recusal last July, said that her directions were procedural in nature and were made in the interest of managing a case that has seen prolonged delays since its filing in 2021. Meanwhile, Najib is appealing High Court judge Alice Loke Yee Ching’s decision not to cite Terrirudin for contempt when handling the royal addendum matter when Terrirudin was attorney general. Loke had in September dismissed the former prime minister’s bid to cite Terrirudin for contempt. Najib alleges that the direction given by Terrirudin was to advance false arguments and deny the existence of the "addendum order". “In the absence of clear evidence showing that the respondent personally did as alleged... these allegations are but mere speculation,” the judge said in dismissing Najib’s application. Wong, who sat with appellate judges Datuk Mohd Firuz Jaffril and Datuk Nadzarin Wok Nordin, on Friday allowed Najib’s application. This came after Wan Arfan did not object to Wong and Firuz’s disclosure over possible conflict of interest, as Wong’s wife was still in the Attorney General’s Chambers when Ahmad Terrirudin was AG, and Firuz had also presided and written the majority decision in the Court of Appeal with regard to Najib’s addendum appeal decided on Jan 6 last year. Najib is currently serving his six-year jail sentence after being found guilty over the SRC International Sdn Bhd case for criminal breach of trust, money laundering, and abuse of power. He had also been given a RM50 million fine for that conviction. Najib has also been convicted for four abuse of power and 21 money laundering charges with regard to a 1Malaysia Development Bhd case where he has been sentenced to another 15 years’ jail, which the politician is appealing. title: MACC to target agents, middlemen as main enablers of corruption in ongoing immigration, JPJ crackdown
body: GENTING HIGHLANDS (Feb 13): The Malaysian Anti-Corruption Commission (MACC) said it will shift its enforcement focus this year towards targeting agents, runners and middlemen believed to be the “main enablers” of corruption within government enforcement agencies, including Immigration and the Road Transport Department (JPJ). MACC deputy chief commissioner (operations) Datuk Seri Ahmad Khusairi Yahaya said the move comes after repeated arrests of frontline officers failed to fully address systemic leakages in the entire corruption ecosystem. “From today onwards, I do not want to just arrest Immigration officers. We want to go after the agents — the companies and individuals who bring in foreign workers and act as the real drivers behind these corrupt practices,” he said during the Journalism Workshop: Understanding the MACC in Corruption Prevention and Anti-Corruption Efforts 2026. According to Ahmad Khusairi, enforcement actions in recent years have largely focused on arresting officers within agencies such as Immigration and transport-related departments for the cases related to the JPJ. However, he said the pattern of misconduct continued despite multiple crackdowns. “I am issuing a stern warning for them to cease these activities. We have already identified and gathered intelligence on several syndicates masterminded by these agents, and firm action will be taken,” Ahmad Khusairi said. He described agents and intermediaries as the primary catalysts sustaining corruption networks. In the case of Immigration, he cited instances where foreign workers with blacklist records allegedly paid up to RM6,000 to re-enter Malaysia — with agents reaping substantial profits. “The ones who become rich are the agents. They are the main enablers of corruption,” he said. The MACC will target agents operating at airports and ports, middlemen involved in foreign worker entry arrangements, runners facilitating dealings with JPJ and transport authorities, project lobbyists and intermediaries in government procurement, as well as cartel-linked individuals coordinating multiple company bids. Ahmad Khusairi added that the MACC would also intensify its intelligence-based investigations operation to dismantle syndicates behind enforcement-related corruption. “In procurement cases, we will focus on the middlemen who bring in 10 or 20 companies to form cartels to secure government projects,” he said. He warned that firm action would be taken against those identified. “If we move in, we will go all the way. We will pursue proceeds of crime, including bankruptcy proceedings if necessary, to ensure they can no longer operate businesses in this country,” he said. Several syndicates are already under the MACC’s radar, he added. title: Opinion: China's silver stranglehold — economic warfare in the age of decoupling
body: (Feb 13): Silver has surged approximately 142%-147% in 2025, making it one of the year's best-performing assets. Analysts attribute this to structural supply deficits since 2020, while demand rises from electric vehicles (EVs), solar panels, and artificial intelligence (AI) data centres. However, geopolitical factors and their risks have not been clearly articulated until now. In October 2025, China's Ministry of Commerce announced new licensing requirements for silver exports, starting from Jan 1, 2026, replacing the quota system that has been in place since 2000. China controls between 60% and 70% of the global silver supply through its refining capacity. At the same time, physical inventories in Western vaults have been falling sharply, causing a silver squeeze in the New York-based Commodities Exchange (Comex) and London Bullion Market Assocation (LBMA) markets. In late December 2025, China revealed a White List of 44 Chinese firms authorised to obtain export licences, including all state-owned enterprises and politically connected companies. This impacts global supply chains, financial markets, and the military readiness of its competitors. This illustrates resource nationalism, where a government prioritises domestic companies in distributing strategic resources. Silver is vital to the green economy, AI infrastructure, and digitalisation. Chinese EV manufacturers like BYD, technology companies such as Huawei, and solar producers benefit from preferential access at subsidised rates. By choking off supplies and imposing prohibitive costs on competitors, this pushes out US and allied firms. For years, US companies prided themselves on just-in-time production as a mark of corporate efficiency. However, in the context of US-China geopolitical tensions, this has deadly consequences. Western, Japanese, and South Korean firms have long depended on cheap, reliable Chinese raw materials. This strategy undermines Western "de-risking" and decoupling initiatives, the very policies corporations have spent billions on. Companies like Samsung invested heavily in Texas facilities to reduce reliance on China, but now face stark choices: return to China for materials or stay abroad at crippling costs. This compels firms to rethink their exit strategies from China. The Chinese government utilises its control over raw materials to weaken Western reshoring. The dilemma goes beyond corporations. In late January 2026, UK Prime Minister Starmer visited China, becoming the first British prime minister to do so in eight years. When President Trump warned that doing business with China is "very dangerous", Starmer replied that it would be "foolhardy" not to engage with the world's second-largest economy. Britain secured £2.2 billion (US$3.0 billion or RM11.7 billion) in deals from Beijing during the visit. This marked a public disagreement between the close allies as Western leaders increasingly seek engagement with China despite US warnings. Even America's closest allies find decoupling economically unfeasible when China controls vital resources. This aligns with China's five-year plan, effective from Jan 1, 2026. China's action also acts as a model for Mexico and Peru, the other leading silver suppliers in the world. There is a notable price gap between Shanghai futures and the LBMA and Comex. From late 2025 into early 2026, Shanghai silver traded at significant premiums to Western markets, rising from about US$8 per ounce in late December to US$20-US$25 per ounce by late January 2026. This creates arbitrage opportunities for traders to buy silver more cheaply in London or New York and sell it at higher prices in Shanghai. Even after accounting for transportation costs, profit margins remain attractive. This systematically reduces the silver reserves in LBMA and Comex vaults, which are already dangerously low. London's LBMA vaults contained 31,023 metric tons in June 2022 but had fallen to around 22,126 metric tons by March 2025, a decrease of nearly one-third. Comex registered inventories have dropped by approximately 70% since 2020. Ultimately, prices must align. In deficit scenarios, which fundamentals support Comex and LBMA prices rising to Shanghai levels? Previously, when globalisation was embraced, Comex, the LBMA, and Shanghai markets tracked closely. Current divergence reflects fragmenting global economies. For decades, Comex and the LBMA issued excessive silver futures contracts that were not backed by physical stock. They operated as paper markets, relying on Chinese imports when required. Not anymore. Beijing uses this arbitrage to boost the Shanghai Futures Exchange to rival, or even surpass, London and New York as a global price-setting authority for metals. Failure to meet physical delivery requests undermines the credibility of Comex and the LBMA and accelerates the eastward shift in pricing power. This suggests that China is preparing for a possible military conflict with the US over Taiwan within two to three years. Recent military drills near Taiwan have become more assertive. In December 2025, the Trump administration approved a substantial £10 billion+ arms sale package to Taiwan, the largest-ever single package for the island, which provoked angry responses from China and increased tensions. Officially, China aims for peaceful reunification with Taiwan. If the US economy weakens significantly, Washington may lack the resolve to engage in military conflict. In such conflicts, restricting silver exports, a key component of missile and defence electronics, hampers the US military's capacity to wage war. The US military depends heavily on silver imports for its weapons production. While the US criticises China's coercive policies, it only has itself to blame. China mimics the US strategy by using its control over the manufacturing and supply of strategic metals as a response. If the US restricts technology exports, such as advanced AI chips, it will face retaliation through limitations on strategic materials. Meanwhile, silver prices have been kept artificially low through excessive futures selling. To encourage new investment in silver mines, prices must reflect current supply and demand in fragmented, bifurcated markets. The credibility of the Western financial market is at stake. Comex and the LBMA can no longer subsidise corporate silver demand through paper contracts without causing physical market shortages. For investors, this indicates sustained higher prices as deficits align with geopolitical fragmentation. For corporate leaders, it calls for a radical rethinking of supply chains and a clear understanding of true decoupling costs. For policymakers, it serves as a wake-up call about strategic resource dependencies. The era of cheap silver and assumptions of friendly access to critical materials in integrated global economies is unquestionably over. title: Rafizi claims anti-graft agency preparing raid on him
body: KUALA LUMPUR (Feb 13): Former economy minister Datuk Seri Rafizi Ramli on Friday claimed the country’s anti-graft agency is preparing a raid on him. Citing an unidentified “internal source” within the Malaysian Anti-Corruption Commission (MACC), Rafizi said at a press conference that he is prepared against the “tactics of intimidation and fabrication of cases" used by previous administrations. “Ultimately, the truth will prevail and the people will judge,” he said. His remarks follow a report filed with the MACC by three Malay non-governmental organisations alleging misappropriation linked to a RM1.11 billion investment. The investment involved an agreement signed last March between Malaysia and UK-based semiconductor and software design company ARM Holdings plc, under which the Malaysian government would pay ARM US$250 million (RM1.1 billion) over 10 years in exchange for its intellectual property licences and computer subsystems (CSS). These assets are intended to be made available to domestic companies in the electrical and electronics sector. Rafizi was the economy minister at the time but resigned from the Cabinet two months later after losing the PKR deputy president race. Since then, he has been a vocal government critic, including on the recent controversy involving MACC chief Tan Sri Azam Baki, who is alleged to have held shares in a company above the limit allowed for civil servants. Following the NGOs’ report, the MACC said it would review the documents and evidence submitted before deciding on further investigations. On Friday, Rafizi said he is prepared to face arrest, raids, or detention if authorities proceed, describing himself as a “veteran” in dealing with such measures. “If I have to go in and be handcuffed, it is worth it for matters important to the rakyat,” he said. He added that he has not yet been contacted by the MACC for a statement recording and urged the agency to “revisit the plan,” warning that current actions could backfire on the public. Rafizi stressed that the ARM deal had been vetted by the Cabinet and that disbursement of funds falls under the Ministry of Investment, Trade and Industry. “This is merely a perception war. What they are doing is to sully my reputation. If you have done nothing wrong, and it is the truth, Insya Allah, you will be safe,” he said. title: US, Taiwan finalise deal to cut tariffs, boost purchases of US goods
body: WASHINGTON/TAIPEI (Feb 12): Trump administration officials signed a final reciprocal trade agreement that confirmed a 15% US tariff rate for imports from Taiwan, while committing Taiwan to a schedule for eliminating or lowering tariffs on nearly all US goods. The document released by the US Trade Representative's office on Thursday also commits Taiwan to significantly boost purchases of US goods from 2025 through 2029, including US$44.4 billion of liquefied natural gas and crude oil, US$15.2 billion of civil aircraft and engines, US$25.2 billion of power grid equipment and generators, marine and steelmaking equipment. The agreement adds technical language and specific details to a trade framework deal first reached in January that cut tariffs on Taiwanese goods, including from its powerhouse semiconductor industries, to 15% from the 20% initially imposed by Trump. That puts Taiwan on an equal footing with its closest Asian export competitors, South Korea and Japan. "This is a pivotal moment for Taiwan's economy and industries to ride the winds of change and undergo a major transformation," Taiwan President Lai Ching-te wrote on his Facebook page. It will optimise the Taiwan–US economic and trade framework, build trustworthy industrial supply chains and establish a Taiwan-US high-tech strategic partnership, he added. Taiwan also won exemptions from reciprocal tariffs for more than 2,000 product items exported to the United States, meaning the average tariff on US exports will drop to 12.33%, Lai said. The deal will need approval by Taiwan's parliament, where the opposition has a majority. The January agreement included a pledge by Taiwan that its companies would invest US$250 billion to boost production of semiconductors, energy and artificial intelligence in the US, including US$100 billion already committed by Taiwan Semiconductor Manufacturing Corp. The Taiwan government would guarantee another US$250 billion in US investments, Commerce Secretary Howard Lutnick said. The final language did not provide further details on those investments, but said Taiwan's representative office in the U.S. would collaborate with US authorities to facilitate additional new greenfield and brownfield investments "in strategic high-technology manufacturing sectors, including AI, semiconductors, and advanced electronics." The deal will immediately eliminate Taiwan's tariffs of up to 26% on many US agricultural imports, including beef, dairy and corn. But some tariffs, including the current 40% tariff on pork belly and 32% on ham, will only fall to 10%, according to the tariff schedule. The US said that under the deal, Taiwan will remove non-tariff barriers on motor vehicles and accept US auto safety standards, as well as those on medical devices and pharmaceuticals. US Trade Representative Jamieson Greer said in a statement that the agreement will boost export opportunities for US farmers, ranchers, fishermen, workers, and manufacturers. "This agreement also builds on our longstanding economic and trade relationship with Taiwan and will significantly enhance the resilience of our supply chains, particularly in high-technology sectors," Greer added. For the first 11 months of 2025, the US trade deficit with Taiwan ballooned to US$126.9 billion from US$73.7 billion for all of 2024, largely due to the large increase in imports of high-end AI chips from Taiwan, according to US Census Bureau data. title: Trump's DOJ antitrust head steps down after turbulent tenure
body: LOS ANGELES/WASHINGTON (Feb 12): The head of the US Justice Department's antitrust division stepped down on Thursday, less than a year after being appointed by President Donald Trump, marking the highest profile casualty in a battle within the administration over policing anti-competitive conduct. Gail Slater, a veteran antitrust attorney, was confirmed in March to head the division, which enforces laws against illegal monopolies. She said on X that it was "with great sadness and abiding hope" that she was leaving on Thursday. "It was indeed the honour of a lifetime to serve in this role," she added. Slater's move throws the division into uncertainty as companies facing antitrust probes have increasingly hired Trump-connected lobbyists to influence the outcomes of their cases. It leaves the division with few senior leaders, following the departure of its head of civil litigation this week. The news of her departure boosted shares in Ticketmaster owner Live Nation, which ended the day up by 2.5%. The antitrust division has sued the company, accusing it of dominating live entertainment markets. Semafor reported earlier this week that Live Nation lobbyists were negotiating with senior DOJ officials outside the antitrust division to avoid trial. Dozens of states are also suing Live Nation, and a DOJ settlement would not end their claims. In a statement, US Attorney General Pam Bondi said, “On behalf of the Department of Justice, we thank Gail Slater for her service to the Antitrust Division which works to protect consumers, promote affordability, and expand economic opportunity.” Deputy Assistant Attorney General Omeed Assefi, who leads criminal enforcement, will take over as acting head of the division. Spokespeople for the White House and for Vice President JD Vance, who Slater advised during his time in the Senate, declined to comment. In July, Reuters and other outlets reported two of Slater's deputies were fired for insubordination after Slater pushed back on orders to settle a case that would have blocked Hewlett Packard Enterprise's US$14 billion acquisition of Juniper Networks. The move exposed a power struggle within the Trump administration between proponents of robust antitrust enforcement and dealmakers seeking to leverage influence. Roger Alford, one of the fired officials, said afterwards in a speech that two DOJ officials outside the antitrust division had "perverted justice" and acted inconsistently with the rule of law in connection with the settlement. He warned that lobbyists were jeopardising the antitrust division's efforts to protect Trump's working class base. "MAGA-in-name-only lobbyists are influencing their allies within the DOJ and risking President Trump's populist conservative agenda," Alford said. Mike Davis, a Trump ally and former counsel to Republican Senator Chuck Grassley, advised HPE on the settlement. Davis also advised Live Nation on its negotiations with the DOJ, according to Semafor. And he was hired by Compass, the nation's largest residential real estate broker, to avert a DOJ investigation into its bid to acquire rival Anywhere Real Estate, the Wall Street Journal reported in January. "Good riddance," Davis posted on social media site X about Slater's departure. Senator Elizabeth Warren, a Democrat from Massachusetts, issued a statement calling for a congressional investigation of Slater's departure. Both the US House and Senate are currently controlled by Republicans. “Every antitrust case in front of the Trump Justice Department now reeks of double-dealing," Warren said. Slater previously worked in the White House during Trump's first term. She also worked for a decade as an antitrust lawyer at the Federal Trade Commission, where she brought cases to block mergers including Whole Foods' acquisition of organic grocer Wild Oats. Slater, who was born in Ireland, did stints as an executive at Fox Corp and Roku. Last year, Slater wrote that the "main thing" for her office was focusing on the average American's biggest expenditures. Housing, transportation, food, healthcare and utilities led the list, according to a pie chart Slater posted on X. Prioritising those issues was "America First antitrust," she wrote. The DOJ launched probes into egg producers and the meatpacking industry last year, and required US power company Constellation Energy to divest three power plants in order to complete its US$16.4 billion acquisition of Calpine Corporation. Her division continued the US crackdown on Big Tech companies that started during Trump's first term, with major cases against Alphabet's Google and Apple. The antitrust division is currently reviewing Netflix's proposed US$82.7 billion deal to buy Warner Bros Discovery's studio and streaming assets, Paramount Skydance's rival bid, and Getty Images acquisition of rival Shutterstock, along with many other deals. title: Malaysia’s anti-graft chief Azam Baki says open to being investigated
body: KUALA LUMPUR (Feb 13): Malaysia’s anti-graft agency chief Tan Sri Azam Baki said he is open to being investigated by any committee established by the government to examine his shareholdings. Azam, who is the chief commissioner of the Malaysian Anti-Corruption Commission (MACC), reiterated in a personal statement that he has made the necessary declarations through official channels based on current regulations governing public service officers. “I have nothing to hide,” he said. “I welcome any transparent, independent and objective process to ascertain the facts based on evidence and in accordance with the principles of justice and the rule of law.” The statement comes amid simmering public outrage following news report of his outsized holdings in shares of public listed companies. Bloomberg first reported of his ownership of 17.7 million shares in financial services firm Velocity Capital Partner Bhd (KL: VELOCITY ). In a press conference reported by national news agency Bernama , Azam has acknowledged of buying the shares in early 2025 before selling them in July. He has also said he is taking legal action against Bloomberg . "We stand by our reporting,” a Bloomberg News spokesperson said in an email to The Edge . Azam also said he will fully cooperate with any investigations, adding that he is confident that “the truth will prevail through a fair and independent process”. title: Oversight panel calls for MACC to reopen 136 'no further action' cases, citing probe flaws
body: GENTING HIGHLANDS (Feb 13): The Operations Evaluation Panel (PPO), an independent oversight body monitoring the Malaysian Anti-Corruption Commission (MACC), said it has recommended the reopening of 136 investigation papers classified as “no further action” (NFA) over the past 16 years, citing investigative weaknesses and overlooked leads. Statistics presented by the panel showed that of the 1,896 NFA cases recorded from 2009 to 2025 by the anti-graft agency, 1,760 investigation papers were formally reviewed by the PPO. Following its assessment, 136 cases — representing 7.7% of those scrutinised — were recommended for reinvestigation. “Our assessment is conducted from several perspectives. First, we determine whether there were weaknesses in the investigation that need to be addressed. If we find shortcomings, we provide advice on how the investigation can be improved,” PPO chairman Datuk Ahmad Rosli Mohd Sham told reporters. He said some cases may have overlooked certain investigative angles, while others might not have disclosed offences under corruption laws but pointed to possible alternative offences under other statutes. “In many cases, the outcome depends on the investigating officer’s own capacity and perspective, which is shaped by the information available to them,” he added. The data were presented at the Journalism Workshop: Understanding MACC in Corruption Prevention and Anti-Corruption Efforts 2026, organised by the MACC’s Strategic Communications Division, where Ahmad Rosli outlined the panel’s supervisory role. Statistics shown during the session indicated that the number of NFA cases reviewed fluctuated annually, with higher volumes recorded in the early years — particularly 2009 and 2010 — before moderating in subsequent years. While most cases reviewed were maintained as NFA, a consistent number each year were recommended for further action. The PPO is one of five independent oversight bodies established under the MACC Act 2009 to enhance institutional accountability. The others are the Anti-Corruption Advisory Board, the Special Committee on Corruption, the Complaints Committee, and the Consultation and Corruption Prevention Panel. Members of the PPO are appointed by the Prime Minister Datuk Seri Anwar Ibrahim and do not serve within the MACC. The panel does not conduct investigations but evaluates whether investigations were properly carried out. The disclosures come amid continued public concern over the MACC’s institutional independence and its handling of high-profile cases. Civil society organisations and legal observers have in recent years called for structural reforms, including clearer separation between the roles of the attorney general and public prosecutor, stronger parliamentary oversight, and greater transparency in decisions to classify cases as NFA. While the PPO does not possess prosecutorial authority, its recommendations can lead to reinvestigations or expanded probes when investigative gaps are identified, serving as an additional layer of scrutiny within Malaysia’s anti-corruption framework. “One of our recommendations has been to enhance the capability of their officers (the MACC). In handling complex cases, particularly corporate investigations, officers need expertise in corporate law and business transactions. When investigating matters involving shares and corporate dealings, there are specific methods and indicators to detect irregularities,” Ahmad Rosli added. Among the matters reported to the PPO are the percentage of investigation papers completed within stipulated timeframes, compliance with internal targets — generally investigations should not exceed 12 months — as well as the duration of remand periods. title: Senator says El Paso airport shutdown shows coordination problem between FAA, Pentagon
body: WASHINGTON (Feb 13): The top Democrat on the Senate Commerce Committee said on Thursday the brief shutdown of El Paso airport by the Federal Aviation Administration (FAA) because of safety concerns posed by the use of a military laser-based anti-drone system was unacceptable. The FAA moved late on Tuesday to shut down the Texas airport for 10 days after the Pentagon vowed to move ahead with deploying the anti-drone system without completing a safety analysis, only to reverse course early on Wednesday and lift the shutdown after about eight hours. "We have a real problem of coordination between DOD and FAA, so we need to resolve that," Senator Maria Cantwell said at a hearing. The sudden closure of the nation's 71st busiest airport by the FAA stranded air travellers and disrupted medical evacuation flights overnight. The FAA initially said the closure of the airport handling four million passengers yearly was for "special security reasons". The 10-day shutdown would have been an unprecedented action involving a single airport. Government and airline officials, speaking on condition of anonymity, said the FAA closed the airspace due to concerns that an Army laser-based counter-drone system could pose risks to air traffic. The two agencies had planned to discuss the issue on Feb 20, but the Army opted to proceed without FAA approval, sources said, which prompted the FAA to halt flights. Commerce Committee chair Ted Cruz, a Republican senator from Texas, said he wants a classified briefing to understand what happened. US Transportation Secretary Sean Duffy, who oversees the FAA, said the closure had been prompted by a drone incursion by a Mexican drug cartel. However, a drone sighting near an airport would typically lead to a brief pause on traffic, not an extended closure. The Pentagon says there are more than 1,000 such incidents each month along the US-Mexico border. Uploaded by Felyx Teoh Copyright © 1999- 2026 The Edge Communications Sdn. title: Amirudin calls for clearer SOPs on unlawful houses of worship in Selangor
body: SHAH ALAM (Feb 13): Selangor Menteri Besar Datuk Seri Amirudin Shari has ordered improvements to existing state government procedures regarding illegal houses of worship on state-owned land. He said immediate action at the local authority level, along with clearer standard operating procedures (SOPs) for the Selangor Five Religions Houses of Worship Committee (Limas), must be implemented. “For houses of worship occupying private land, the existing process requires the landowner to appoint a lawyer to obtain a court order to enable any eviction and demolition to take place. “No party should take the law into their own hands without going through the court process. This is in accordance with the National Land Code and land-related laws,” he said in a statement on Thursday night. Amirudin said that in view of safety considerations, the Selangor State Security Council (MKN) has decided that landowners who find that trespassing has occurred and that a house of worship has been built without approval must lodge a police report. “This will allow the Royal Malaysian Police (PDRM) to investigate and, if proven, the prosecution process for the offence of trespassing will commence. "Secondly, landowners should send a notice to the trespassers and formally inform the District Office. The District Security Committee (JKD), chaired by the District Officer, has been activated in all districts in Selangor,” he said. Amirudin said the JKD would act as a mediator by summoning all parties, including landowners, owners of the houses of worship, PDRM and local authorities, to reach a reasonable solution. “Should this process fail to yield results, the JKD will advise the landowner to proceed with court action. This approach ensures the entire process involves the authorities and prevents any incidents that could trigger unrest,” he added. Earlier n Thursday, Amirudin chaired the Selangor MKN meeting, attended by Selangor police chief Datuk Shazeli Kahar, the Commander of the 11th Brigade headquarters, council presidents and district officers, to discuss the state's public security situation. “This follows the issue concerning houses of worship, which has sparked differing opinions from various parties. The police are investigating an incident in Rawang yesterday [Wednesday], and it will go through the appropriate legal process. “The incident in Rawang has caused unease and concern among the people. This must be addressed immediately to prevent any incident that could threaten the state's racial and religious harmony,” he said. Through the meeting, he said that overall, there are two main issues involving unlawful houses of worship: those occupying state-owned land and those built on private land.
